text:
alex: quick check — I prototyped a tenant-scoped handoff that prefers standby-quorum when local health < 60% and any remote region has >= 70% healthy replicas. added a 30s grace window; need eyes before I land it.

maria: paste the prototype config? want to see the knobs.

alex: sure — config I ran in staging: 
```
handoff_policy:
  remote_ready_pct: 70
  local_unhealthy_pct: 60
  initial_grace_secs: 30
  backoff_base_secs: 30
  backoff_cap_secs: 300
  per_tenant_anti_thrash_secs: 600
  require_telemetry_stable: true
```

kevin: :eyes: two quick flags — autoscaling reactions could be slower than 30s, and we need a cross-region coordination guard to avoid N regions flipping at once.

alex: added exponential backoff and per-tenant anti-thrash window (defaults above). also added a coordination token so only one region proceeds with handoff for a tenant at a time.

maria: how do you compute "healthy"? p50/p90 latency? error rate? node count?

alex: composite signal: p90 latency < tenant_config.latency_slo AND error_rate < tenant_config.err_pct AND live_replicas >= replica_threshold. we tag which sub-signal failed so ops can filter.

kevin: please add consecutive-sample requirement (circuit) to avoid single-sample flips.

alex: implemented 3 consecutive windows across a 15s rolling window. emits attempt event to ops and increments a metric: handoff_attempts.

infra-bot: webhook: tenant-scoped-handoff prototype deployed to staging (img: rgw/handoff:v0.3) — rollout ok :white_check_mark:

maria: test plan: simulate slow region (p90 ~200ms) + 2% error spike; ensure no handoff until both conditions persist for 3 samples and anti-thrash prevents rapid reflip. I'll run sims this afternoon.

sre-oncall: FYI — when you run canary, post tenant ids and enable synthetic probes for those tenants. I'll watch for routing churn.

alex: noted. metric added: handoff_reason tag values = [latency, errors, node_loss, replica_drop]. also added handoff_owner_region tag.

kevin: consider adding a "safe-fallback" model: if handoff fails mid-way, we should revert to local read-only mode rather than full write acceptance in fallback region. saves consistency issues.

alex: good idea. I added transitional state 'fenced-reads' that lets the client know writes are temporarily disabled for that tenant and retries to primary. ops event emitted if we enter that state.

maria: runbook note: canary criteria = 0.5% increase in 5m write latency OR any consumer-visible error > 0.1% for canary tenants -> rollback. also require manual approval for Dedicated canary.

sre-oncall: add synthetic probes with write+read verification and tag them by canary-tenant. I'll subscribe alerts to the oncall channel.

alex: done. next steps: PR with docs + runbook, run sims, small Dedicated canary next week if staging green.

maria: I'll post sim results and tenant ids here once done.

kevin: one last ask — add a metric for "handoff_duration_ms" and "handoff_outcome" (success|aborted|reverted). will help postmortems.

alex: added both. thanks all.

sre-oncall: ping me right before canary window starts. I'll be on-call.

alex: will do. PR incoming after I tidy logs and add a short swagger for the coordination endpoint.
